source.text: צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אָרִ֖יב אֵלֶ֑יךָ אַ֤ךְ מִשְׁפָּטִים֙ אֲדַבֵּ֣ר אוֹתָ֔ךְ מַדּ֗וּעַ דֶּ֤רֶךְ רְשָׁעִים֙ צָלֵ֔חָה שָׁל֖וּ כָּל־בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: Righteous [are] you, Yahweh, when I bring a case to you; yet judgments I will speak with you: why [does the] way of wicked [ones] prosper, [why] are at ease all [who] betray [with] betrayal?

en.L: Righteous [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, when I bring a case to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q yet I will speak judgments with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}: \q Why does [the] way of [the] wicked prosper? \q [Why] are all who betray [with] betrayal at ease?
en.B: You are in the right, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, whenever I bring a case against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q still, I must set my charges before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}: \q Why does the way of the wicked succeed? \q Why do all the faithless live untroubled?
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are righteous; when I argue with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are always in the right. \q But I still want to ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} about what is fair. \q Why do wicked people do so well? \q Why do people who are never loyal to anyone live without a care?

es.L: Justo [eres] {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, cuando litigo contigo; \q sin embargo, hablaré contigo de juicios: \q ¿Por qué prospera el camino de los malvados? \q ¿[Por qué] viven tranquilos todos los que traicionan con traición?
es.B: Tienes la razón, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, siempre que presento un pleito contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}; \q aun así, tengo que exponerte mis quejas: \q ¿Por qué tiene éxito el camino de los malvados? \q ¿Por qué viven sin preocupaciones todos los traidores?
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres justo; cuando discuto contigo, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} siempre tienes la razón. \q Pero aun así quiero preguntar{{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} qué es lo justo. \q ¿Por qué les va tan bien a los malvados? \q ¿Por qué viven tan tranquilos los que nunca son leales a nadie?

fr.L: Juste [es]-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, quand je plaide contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; \q pourtant je veux parler de jugements avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} : \q Pourquoi la voie des méchants prospère-t-elle ? \q [Pourquoi] tous les traîtres qui trahissent sont-ils en paix ?
fr.B: Tu as raison, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, chaque fois que je plaide contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; \q pourtant, je dois porter devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} mes griefs : \q Pourquoi le chemin des méchants réussit-il ? \q Pourquoi tous les infidèles vivent-ils tranquilles ?
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es juste ; quand je discute avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, c’est toujours {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui as raison. \q Mais je veux quand même {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} poser une question sur ce qui est juste. \q Pourquoi les méchants réussissent-ils si bien ? \q Pourquoi les gens qui ne sont fidèles à personne vivent-ils sans souci ?

sw.L: Wewe [u] mwenye haki, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ninapoleta shauri {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}; \q hata hivyo nitasema nawe habari za hukumu: \q Mbona njia ya waovu inafanikiwa? \q [Mbona] wote wanaotenda hila kwa hila wanastarehe?
sw.B: Wewe u mwenye haki, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kila ninapoleta shauri dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}; \q hata hivyo, sina budi kuyaweka mashtaka yangu mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}: \q Mbona njia ya waovu inafanikiwa? \q Mbona wote wasio waaminifu wanaishi bila taabu?
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mwenye haki; ninapobishana nawe, daima {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uko sawa. \q Lakini bado nataka kukuuliza kuhusu haki. \q Kwa nini watu waovu wanafanikiwa sana? \q Kwa nini watu wasio waaminifu kwa mtu yeyote wanaishi bila wasiwasi?

vi.L: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] công chính khi con trình việc kiện lên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q dù vậy con vẫn xin trình bày lý lẽ với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: \q Tại sao đường lối kẻ ác lại thịnh vượng? \q [Tại sao] mọi kẻ phản bội [cách] gian trá lại được yên ổn?
vi.B: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, mỗi khi con đem việc kiện đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} luôn là công chính; \q dù vậy, con vẫn phải trình bày lý lẽ của con trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: \q Tại sao đường lối kẻ ác lại hanh thông? \q Tại sao mọi kẻ bội tín lại sống yên ổn?
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là công chính; khi con tranh luận với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} luôn luôn đúng. \q Nhưng con vẫn muốn hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về lẽ công bằng. \q Tại sao kẻ ác lại làm ăn thịnh đạt? \q Tại sao những kẻ chẳng trung tín với ai lại sống vô tư lự?

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님께 소송을 할 때에 주님은 의로우십니다. \q 그래도 제가 주님과 함께 판결들을 말하겠습니다. \q 어찌하여 악인들의 길이 형통합니까? \q 배신을 일삼는 자들이 모두 어찌하여 평안합니까?
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 제가 주님께 따질 때마다 주님은 언제나 옳으십니다. \q 그래도 제가 주님 앞에 제 고소를 내놓겠습니다. \q 어찌하여 악인들의 길이 잘됩니까? \q 어찌하여 신의 없는 자들이 모두 근심 없이 삽니까?
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님은 의로우십니다. 제가 주님과 따져도 언제나 주님이 옳으십니다. \q 그래도 무엇이 공정한지 주님께 여쭙고 싶습니다. \q 어찌하여 악한 사람들이 그렇게 잘삽니까? \q 어찌하여 누구에게도 신의를 지키지 않는 사람들이 걱정 없이 삽니까?

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's prayer goes on from 11:18-23
decisions.reason: The chapter division falls in the middle of one of Jeremiah's prayers to God, which began at 11:18. He has just learned of the plot against his life by the people of his home town (11:21-23); now he turns to the larger question it raises. God answers in verses 5-6.

decisions.choice: righteous ... bring a case ... judgments: the language of a court
decisions.reason: "Righteous" here is the word for the party who is in the right in a lawsuit. The verb is the one used for bringing a legal complaint, and "judgments" are the points of a case. Jeremiah grants at the start that God will be found in the right, yet he still wants to argue his complaint (compare Job 23:3-7; Habakkuk 1:2-4, 13).

decisions.choice: all who betray with betrayal: people utterly treacherous
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun from the same root are set side by side for emphasis: people whose whole way of life is breaking faith. The same verb returns in verse 6 for Jeremiah's own family.

decisions.choice: You are in the right ... set my charges before you
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the court picture: "in the right" is what "righteous" means in a lawsuit, and "charges" are what Jeremiah wants to argue.

decisions.choice: argue with you ... what is fair ... never loyal to anyone
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "righteous" and then says plainly what a court case means; "never loyal to anyone" explains the doubled word for betrayal.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's lament continued, God addressed as "tú"
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's prayer of 11:18-23 goes on; he speaks to God as "tú", in the language of a lawsuit, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Wewe at the head of the line
decisions.reason: A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital (style guide), so the opening "Wewe" takes no span; the prayer goes on from 11:18-23 without quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's lament (11:18-12:6) addressed to God with "tu" and the deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's laments are his prayers; God is addressed as "tu", as in the Psalms, and the court picture of "plaider" is kept at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's prayer continues: "lạy CHÚA", "Ngài", "con"
decisions.reason: His lament goes on from 11:18-23 to verse 4, in the prayer forms of the terms note; God's answer from verse 5 says "ngươi" (Literal) and "con" (Balanced, Readable) to him, as in chapter 1.

source.text: נְטַעְתָּם֙ גַּם־שֹׁרָ֔שׁוּ יֵלְכ֖וּ גַּם־עָ֣שׂוּ פֶ֑רִי קָר֤וֹב אַתָּה֙ בְּפִיהֶ֔ם וְרָח֖וֹק מִכִּלְיוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: You planted them, also they have taken root; they go, also they have made fruit; near [are] you in their mouth and far from their kidneys.

en.L: You planted them; they have even taken root; \q they go on; they even produce fruit. \q Near [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in their mouth, \q and far from their kidneys.
en.B: You planted them, and they have taken root; \q they flourish and bear fruit. \q You are near in their mouths \q but far from their inmost being.
en.R: You planted them, and they put down roots. \q They grow and produce fruit. \q They talk about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all the time, \q but deep inside they do not care about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at all.

es.L: Los plantaste; también echaron raíces; \q crecen; también dan fruto. \q Cerca [estás] {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} de su boca, \q y lejos de sus riñones.
es.B: Los plantaste, y han echado raíces; \q prosperan y dan fruto. \q Estás cerca de sus labios, \q pero lejos de lo más íntimo de su ser.
es.R: Los plantaste, y echaron raíces. \q Crecen y dan fruto. \q Hablan de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} todo el tiempo, \q pero en el fondo no les importas nada.

fr.L: Tu les as plantés ; ils ont même pris racine ; \q ils avancent ; ils portent même du fruit. \q Proche [es]-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} de leur bouche, \q et loin de leurs reins.
fr.B: Tu les as plantés, et ils ont pris racine ; \q ils prospèrent et portent du fruit. \q Tu es près de leur bouche, \q mais loin de leur cœur.
fr.R: Tu les as plantés, et ils ont fait des racines. \q Ils grandissent et ils donnent des fruits. \q Ils parlent de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} sans arrêt, \q mais au fond d’eux-mêmes, ils ne se soucient pas du tout de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

sw.L: Uliwapanda; wameota mizizi pia; \q wanaendelea; wanazaa matunda pia. \q Wewe [u] karibu vinywani mwao, \q na mbali na figo zao.
sw.B: Uliwapanda, nao wametia mizizi; \q wanastawi na kuzaa matunda. \q Uko karibu vinywani mwao \q lakini mbali na mioyo yao.
sw.R: Uliwapanda, nao wakatia mizizi. \q Wanakua na kuzaa matunda. \q Wanazungumza habari {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} kila wakati, \q lakini ndani yao hawakujali hata kidogo.

vi.L: Ngài đã trồng chúng; chúng cũng đã đâm rễ; \q chúng lớn lên; chúng cũng đã ra trái. \q Ngài ở gần miệng chúng, \q nhưng xa lòng dạ chúng.
vi.B: Ngài đã trồng chúng, và chúng đã đâm rễ; \q chúng lớn mạnh và sinh trái. \q Miệng chúng thì gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q nhưng lòng dạ chúng lại xa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ngài đã trồng chúng, và chúng đã đâm rễ. \q Chúng lớn lên và sinh trái. \q Chúng luôn nhắc đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q nhưng tận trong lòng chúng chẳng quan tâm gì đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cả.

ko.L: 주님께서 그들을 심으셨으므로 그들이 뿌리를 내렸고, \q 자라서 열매도 맺었습니다. \q 그들의 입에는 주님이 가까이 계시지만 \q 그들의 콩팥에서는 멀리 계십니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 그들을 심으시니 그들이 뿌리를 내리고 \q 무성하게 자라 열매를 맺습니다. \q 그들의 입에는 주님이 가까이 계시지만 \q 그들의 속마음에서는 멀리 계십니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 그들을 심으시니 그들이 뿌리를 내렸습니다. \q 그들은 자라서 열매를 맺습니다. \q 그들은 늘 주님에 대해 말하지만 \q 속으로는 주님께 전혀 관심이 없습니다.

decisions.choice: planted ... taken root ... fruit: the wicked pictured as a thriving plant
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's complaint is that God himself planted these people and lets them grow. God had used the same picture of Israel, planted as a choice vine (2:21; 11:16-17).

decisions.choice: near in their mouth, far from their kidneys: they speak of God but do not hold him inwardly
decisions.reason: The kidneys were thought of as the seat of a person's deepest feelings and motives, often paired with the heart (11:20; 17:10; Psalm 7:10). God's name is always on their lips, but he has no place in their inner life (compare Isaiah 29:13).

decisions.choice: inmost being (Balanced); deep inside (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "kidneys" rather than the body part, which would puzzle a modern reader. Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: They talk about you all the time
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "near in their mouth": God is often in their talk.

decisions.choice: figo (Literal); mioyo (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The kidneys are the seat of the inmost feelings (meaning decision m2); Literal keeps the body word as the Hebrew, Balanced uses "moyo", the Swahili seat of feeling.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יְדַעְתָּ֔נִי תִּרְאֵ֕נִי וּבָחַנְתָּ֥ לִבִּ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ הַתִּקֵם֙ כְּצֹ֣אן לְטִבְחָ֔ה וְהַקְדִּשֵׁ֖ם לְי֥וֹם הֲרֵגָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, Yahweh, you know me; you see me, and you test my heart with you; drag them off like sheep for slaughter, and set them apart for [a] day of killing.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know me; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see me, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} test my heart [toward] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Drag them off like sheep for slaughter, \q and set them apart for [the] day of killing.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, know me; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} see me \q and test how my heart stands toward {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Drag them away like sheep to be slaughtered; \q set them apart for the day of killing.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}. You see me. \q You test my heart and see how I feel about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Drag those wicked people away like sheep to be killed. \q Set them aside for the day when they will be slaughtered.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me conoces; {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me ves, \q y pruebas mi corazón [para] contigo. \q Arrástralos como ovejas al matadero, \q y apártalos para el día de la matanza.
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, me conoces; {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me ves \q y examinas cómo está mi corazón contigo. \q Arrástralos como ovejas al matadero; \q apártalos para el día de la matanza.
es.R: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me conoces, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Me ves. \q Pones a prueba mi corazón y ves lo que siento por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. \q Arrastra a esos malvados como ovejas al matadero. \q Apártalos para el día en que serán sacrificados.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me connais ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me vois, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} éprouves mon cœur [qui est] avec {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. \q Entraîne-les comme des brebis à l’abattoir, \q et mets-les à part pour le jour du massacre.
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me connais ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me vois \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais ce qu’est mon cœur envers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. \q Entraîne-les comme des moutons qu’on va égorger ; \q réserve-les pour le jour du massacre.
fr.R: Mais {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me connais. Tu me vois. \q Tu éprouves mon cœur et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vois ce que je ressens pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. \q Emmène ces méchants comme des moutons qu’on va tuer. \q Garde-les pour le jour où ils seront massacrés.

sw.L: Nawe, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, unanijua; unaniona, \q na unaujaribu moyo wangu [ulivyo] {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}. \q Wakokote kama kondoo wa kuchinjwa, \q na uwatenge kwa siku ya kuuawa.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, unanijua; unaniona \q na kuujaribu moyo wangu ulivyo {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}. \q Wakokote kama kondoo wa kuchinjwa; \q uwatenge kwa siku ya machinjo.
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unanijua, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Unaniona. \q Unaujaribu moyo wangu na kuona jinsi ninavyokuhisi. \q Wakokote watu hao waovu kama kondoo wanaopelekwa kuchinjwa. \q Watenge kwa ajili ya siku watakapochinjwa.

vi.L: Còn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết con; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy con, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thử lòng con [đối với] {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Xin kéo chúng đi như chiên bị đem làm thịt, \q và biệt riêng chúng cho ngày tàn sát.
vi.B: Nhưng lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết con; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy con \q và thử nghiệm lòng con đối với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thế nào. \q Xin kéo chúng đi như chiên bị đem làm thịt; \q xin biệt riêng chúng ra cho ngày tàn sát.
vi.R: Nhưng lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết con. Ngài thấy con. \q Ngài thử lòng con và biết con nghĩ gì về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Xin kéo những kẻ ác ấy đi như chiên bị đem đi giết. \q Xin để riêng chúng ra cho ngày chúng bị tàn sát.

ko.L: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님은 저를 아시고 저를 보시며, \q 주님을 향한 제 마음을 시험하십니다. \q 그들을 도살할 양처럼 끌어내시고, \q 죽일 날을 위해 그들을 따로 두십시오.
ko.B: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님은 저를 아시고 저를 보시며, \q 제 마음이 주님을 향해 어떠한지 시험하십니다. \q 저들을 도살할 양처럼 끌어내시고, \q 죽일 날을 위해 따로 떼어 놓으십시오.
ko.R: 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 주님은 저를 아십니다. 주님은 저를 보십니다. \q 주님은 제 마음을 시험하셔서 제가 주님을 어떻게 생각하는지 아십니다. \q 저 악한 사람들을 죽일 양처럼 끌어내십시오. \q 그들이 죽임을 당할 날을 위해 그들을 따로 두십시오.

decisions.choice: test my heart: examine it as metal is tested
decisions.reason: The verb is used for testing metal to find out what it is made of. Jeremiah appeals to God, who has examined his heart and knows it is loyal to him, unlike the people of verse 2 (11:20; 17:10; 20:12).

decisions.choice: sheep for slaughter ... set apart: Jeremiah's own words turned on his enemies
decisions.reason: In 11:19 Jeremiah said he had been like a trusting lamb led to the slaughter. Now he asks that his enemies meet that fate. "Set apart" is the word for making something holy, used of setting animals apart for sacrifice; here it is used with bitter irony for marking the wicked out for death (compare 6:4; 22:7).

decisions.choice: a prayer for judgment, left to God
decisions.reason: Like some psalms (Psalm 109; 137:7-9), Jeremiah asks God to punish his enemies; he does not take revenge himself but leaves the case with God (11:20).

decisions.choice: those wicked people
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are, from verses 1-2.

source.text: עַד־מָתַי֙ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעֵ֥שֶׂב כָּל־הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה יִיבָ֑שׁ מֵרָעַ֣ת יֹֽשְׁבֵי־בָ֗הּ סָפְתָ֤ה בְהֵמוֹת֙ וָע֔וֹף כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ לֹ֥א יִרְאֶ֖ה אֶת־אַחֲרִיתֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Until when will mourn the land, and [the] grass of every field wither? From [the] evil of [those] dwelling in it are swept away animals and bird[s], for they have said, he will not see our end.

en.L: Until when will the land mourn, \q and the grass of every field wither? \q Because of [the] evil of those dwelling in it, \q animals and birds are swept away, \q for they have said, "He will not see our end."
en.B: How long will the land mourn \q and the plants of every field dry up? \q Because of the evil of those who live in it, \q animals and birds have perished, \q for the people say, "He will not see what becomes of us."
en.R: How long will the land be dry and full of sorrow? \q How long will the grass in the fields be dead? \q The animals and birds have died \q because the people who live in the land are evil. \q They say, "He will not see what happens to us in the end."

es.L: ¿Hasta cuándo estará de luto la tierra, \q y se secará la hierba de todo el campo? \q Por la maldad de los que habitan en ella \q han perecido los animales y las aves, \q porque han dicho: «Él no verá nuestro fin».
es.B: ¿Hasta cuándo estará de luto la tierra \q y se secarán las plantas de todo el campo? \q Por la maldad de los que viven en ella \q han perecido animales y aves, \q porque la gente dice: «Él no verá lo que será de nosotros».
es.R: ¿Hasta cuándo estará la tierra seca y llena de tristeza? \q ¿Hasta cuándo estará muerta la hierba de los campos? \q Los animales y las aves han muerto \q porque la gente que vive en el país es malvada. \q Dicen: «Él no verá lo que nos pasará al final».

fr.L: Jusqu’à quand le pays sera-t-il en deuil, \q et l’herbe de tous les champs séchera-t-elle ? \q À cause de la méchanceté de ceux qui l’habitent, \q bêtes et oiseaux disparaissent, \q car ils ont dit : « Il ne verra pas notre fin. »
fr.B: Combien de temps encore le pays sera-t-il en deuil \q et l’herbe de tous les champs desséchée ? \q À cause de la méchanceté de ceux qui l’habitent, \q les bêtes et les oiseaux ont péri, \q car les gens disent : « Il ne verra pas ce que nous allons devenir. »
fr.R: Combien de temps encore le pays sera-t-il sec et plein de tristesse ? \q Combien de temps l’herbe des champs restera-t-elle morte ? \q Les animaux et les oiseaux sont morts \q parce que les gens qui habitent le pays sont méchants. \q Ils disent : « Il ne verra pas ce qui nous arrivera à la fin. »

sw.L: Hata lini nchi itaomboleza, \q na majani ya kila shamba kunyauka? \q Kwa sababu ya uovu wa wakaao ndani yake, \q wanyama na ndege wamefagiliwa mbali, \q kwa maana wamesema, "Hataona mwisho wetu."
sw.B: Nchi itaomboleza hadi lini, \q na mimea ya kila shamba kukauka? \q Kwa sababu ya uovu wa wale wanaoishi ndani yake, \q wanyama na ndege wameangamia, \q kwa maana watu wanasema, "Hataona litakalotupata."
sw.R: Nchi itakuwa kavu na yenye huzuni hadi lini? \q Majani ya mashambani yatakuwa yamekufa hadi lini? \q Wanyama na ndege wamekufa \q kwa sababu watu wanaoishi katika nchi ni waovu. \q Wanasema, "Hataona litakalotupata mwishowe."

vi.L: Cho đến bao giờ đất còn than khóc, \q và cỏ trong mọi đồng ruộng còn khô héo? \q Vì sự gian ác của những kẻ sống trong đó, \q thú vật và chim chóc đều bị quét sạch, \q vì chúng đã nói: "Ông ấy sẽ không thấy kết cuộc của chúng ta."
vi.B: Đất còn than khóc \q và cây cỏ ngoài đồng còn khô héo cho đến bao giờ? \q Vì sự gian ác của những kẻ sống trong đó, \q thú vật và chim chóc đều đã chết hết, \q vì dân chúng nói: "Ông ấy sẽ không thấy chúng ta ra sao đâu."
vi.R: Đất còn khô cằn và đầy sầu khổ đến bao giờ? \q Cỏ ngoài đồng còn chết khô đến bao giờ? \q Thú vật và chim chóc đã chết hết \q vì những người sống trong xứ là gian ác. \q Chúng nói: "Ông ấy sẽ không thấy điều gì xảy đến cho chúng ta sau cùng đâu."

ko.L: 언제까지 이 땅이 슬퍼하며 \q 모든 들의 풀이 시들겠습니까? \q 그 안에 사는 자들의 악 때문에 \q 짐승과 새가 쓸려 갔습니다. \q 그들이 "그는 우리의 마지막을 보지 못할 것이다" 하고 말했기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 언제까지 이 땅이 슬퍼하며 \q 모든 들의 풀이 말라야 합니까? \q 그 땅에 사는 사람들의 악 때문에 \q 짐승과 새들이 멸종했습니다. \q 그들이 "그는 우리가 어떻게 되는지 보지 못할 것이다" 하고 말하기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 언제까지 이 땅이 메마르고 슬픔에 잠겨 있어야 합니까? \q 언제까지 들의 풀이 말라 죽어 있어야 합니까? \q 짐승과 새들이 다 죽었습니다. \q 이 땅에 사는 사람들이 악하기 때문입니다. \q 그들은 "그는 우리가 결국 어떻게 되는지 보지 못할 것이다" 하고 말합니다.

decisions.choice: mourn, with drying up in view
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to mourn, and the land is pictured as grieving (12:11; 23:10; Isaiah 24:4; Hosea 4:3). A word spelled the same way means to dry up, which fits the withered grass in the next line, and both senses may be heard together.

decisions.choice: the land and its creatures suffer for the people's evil
decisions.reason: Drought and the death of animals are among the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:23-24). The people's sin brings harm on the whole land (compare 3:3; 14:1-6; Hosea 4:1-3).

decisions.choice: he will not see our end: who "he" is is left open
alternatives: God will not see our end
the prophet will not live to see our end
decisions.reason: The speakers may mean God: he does not see or care what happens to us. Or they may mean Jeremiah: he will not live to see the ruin he predicts. The Greek translation reads "God will not see our ways". The Hebrew does not say which.

decisions.choice: two "How long" questions; "dry and full of sorrow"
decisions.reason: Readable repeats "How long" for each half of the question and puts both senses of the first verb (see m1) into plain words.

decisions.choice: "Ông ấy" for the one who "will not see our end"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision leaves open who "he" is (God or the prophet); "ông ấy" keeps that open, where "Ngài" would decide for God.

source.text: כִּ֣י אֶת־רַגְלִ֥ים׀רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ וְאֵ֥יךְ תְּתַֽחֲרֶ֖ה אֶת־הַסּוּסִ֑ים וּבְאֶ֤רֶץ שָׁלוֹם֙ אַתָּ֣ה בוֹטֵ֔חַ וְאֵ֥יךְ תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בִּגְא֥וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: For with [men] on foot you have run, and they have wearied you, and how will you compete with the horses? And in [a] land of peace you [are] secure, and how will you do in [the] thicket of the Jordan?

en.L: If you have run with [men] on foot and they have wearied you, \q then how will you compete with horses? \q And [if] in a land of peace you [are] secure, \q then how will you do in the thicket of the Jordan?
en.B: If you have raced with runners on foot and they have worn you out, \q how will you keep pace with horses? \q If you feel secure only in a peaceful land, \q what will you do in the thick brush along the Jordan?
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered me: If you get tired racing against people on foot, \q how will you race against horses? \q If you feel safe only where there is peace, \q what will you do in the thick bushes along the Jordan River, where lions live?

es.L: Si corriste con los de a pie y te cansaron, \q ¿cómo competirás con los caballos? \q Y [si] en tierra de paz te sientes seguro, \q ¿qué harás en la espesura del Jordán?
es.B: Si has corrido con hombres a pie y te han agotado, \q ¿cómo vas a competir con caballos? \q Si solo te sientes seguro en una tierra en paz, \q ¿qué harás en la maleza espesa junto al Jordán?
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me respondió: Si te cansas corriendo contra gente a pie, \q ¿cómo vas a correr contra caballos? \q Si solo te sientes seguro donde hay paz, \q ¿qué harás en los matorrales espesos junto al río Jordán, donde viven los leones?

fr.L: Si avec des piétons tu as couru et qu’ils t’ont fatigué, \q comment rivaliseras-tu avec les chevaux ? \q Et [si] dans un pays de paix tu [te sens] en sécurité, \q comment feras-tu dans les fourrés du Jourdain ?
fr.B: Si tu as couru avec des coureurs à pied et qu’ils t’ont épuisé, \q comment pourras-tu suivre des chevaux ? \q Si tu ne te sens en sécurité que dans un pays paisible, \q que feras-tu dans les broussailles du Jourdain ?
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a répondu : Si tu te fatigues en faisant la course avec des gens à pied, \q comment feras-tu la course avec des chevaux ? \q Si tu ne te sens en sécurité que là où il y a la paix, \q que feras-tu dans les buissons épais le long du Jourdain, où vivent les lions ?

sw.L: Ikiwa umekimbia na [watu] waendao kwa miguu nao wakakuchosha, \q basi utashindanaje na farasi? \q Na [ikiwa] katika nchi ya amani unajiona salama, \q basi utafanyaje katika vichaka vya Yordani?
sw.B: Kama umeshindana mbio na wakimbiaji wa miguu nao wakakuchosha, \q utawezaje kwenda sambamba na farasi? \q Kama unajiona salama katika nchi yenye amani tu, \q utafanya nini katika vichaka vizito kando ya Yordani?
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akanijibu: Ukichoka kushindana mbio na watu wanaotembea kwa miguu, \q utawezaje kushindana mbio na farasi? \q Kama unajiona salama mahali penye amani tu, \q utafanya nini katika vichaka vizito kando ya mto Yordani, wanakoishi simba?

vi.L: Nếu ngươi chạy đua với [người] đi bộ mà họ đã làm ngươi mệt, \q thì làm sao ngươi đua nổi với ngựa? \q Và [nếu] ở trong xứ bình yên ngươi [mới] cảm thấy an toàn, \q thì ngươi sẽ làm gì trong bụi rậm sông Giô-đanh?
vi.B: Nếu con chạy đua với người đi bộ mà họ đã làm con kiệt sức, \q thì làm sao con theo kịp ngựa? \q Nếu chỉ ở trong xứ bình yên con mới thấy an toàn, \q thì con sẽ làm gì trong rừng rậm dọc sông Giô-đanh?
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp lời tôi: Nếu con mệt khi chạy đua với người đi bộ, \q thì làm sao con chạy đua với ngựa được? \q Nếu con chỉ thấy an toàn ở nơi bình yên, \q thì con sẽ làm gì trong những bụi rậm dọc sông Giô-đanh, nơi sư tử sinh sống?

ko.L: 네가 걷는 [사람들과] 달리다가 그들이 너를 지치게 했다면 \q 네가 어떻게 말들과 겨루겠느냐? \q 평안한 땅에서는 네가 안전하다면 \q 요단의 우거진 숲에서는 어떻게 하겠느냐?
ko.B: 네가 걸어서 달리는 사람들과 경주하다가 지쳤다면 \q 어떻게 말들과 겨루겠느냐? \q 네가 평화로운 땅에서만 안전하다고 느낀다면 \q 요단 강가의 우거진 덤불 속에서는 어떻게 하겠느냐?
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 나에게 대답하셨다. 네가 걸어서 달리는 사람들과 경주하다가 지친다면 \q 어떻게 말들과 경주하겠느냐? \q 네가 평화로운 곳에서만 안전하다고 느낀다면 \q 사자들이 사는 요단 강가의 우거진 덤불 속에서는 어떻게 하겠느냐?

decisions.choice: God answers Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Nothing in the Hebrew marks the change of speaker, but the "you" is now Jeremiah, and God replies to his complaint not with an explanation but with a warning that harder trials are coming.

decisions.choice: racing men on foot, then horses: if small troubles tire you, worse ones are ahead
decisions.reason: The picture is of a footrace. If Jeremiah is worn out by the plots so far, how will he cope with greater danger? Verse 6 names the first of it: his own family.

decisions.choice: you are secure
decisions.reason: The usual sense of the word is to trust or feel safe: if Jeremiah can feel safe only in quiet country, how will he manage in the wild? A rarer word spelled the same way means to fall down, which would give "if you stumble in a safe land". The sense of the whole saying is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the thicket of the Jordan: the dense growth along the river, where lions lived
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "the pride of the Jordan": the thick growth of trees and reeds along the river valley. It was wild country where lions had their lairs (49:19; 50:44; Zechariah 11:3).

decisions.choice: The LORD answered me ... the Jordan River, where lions live
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, which the Hebrew leaves to the reader (see m1), and says why the Jordan thicket was dangerous (see m4).

source.text: כִּ֧י גַם־אַחֶ֣יךָ וּבֵית־אָבִ֗יךָ גַּם־הֵ֨מָּה֙ בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ גַּם־הֵ֛מָּה קָרְא֥וּ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ מָלֵ֑א אַל־תַּאֲמֵ֣ן בָּ֔ם כִּֽי־יְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ טוֹבֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For even your brothers and [the] house of your father, even they have dealt treacherously with you; even they have called after you full; do not believe them, though they speak to you good [things].

en.L: For even your brothers and the house of your father, \q even they have dealt treacherously with you; \q even they have called after you [with a] full [voice]. \q Do not trust them, though they speak good [words] to you.
en.B: Your brothers too, the household of your own father, \q even they have broken faith with you; \q they too have raised a loud outcry against you. \q Do not believe them, though they speak kindly to you.
en.R: Even your brothers and the rest of your family \q have turned against you. \q They too are shouting against you. \q Do not trust them, even when they say nice things to you.

es.L: Porque aun tus hermanos y la casa de tu padre, \q aun ellos te han traicionado; \q aun ellos han gritado tras de ti a voz en cuello. \q No les creas, aunque te hablen cosas buenas.
es.B: También tus hermanos, la familia de tu propio padre, \q también ellos te han traicionado; \q también ellos han levantado un gran clamor contra ti. \q No les creas, aunque te hablen con amabilidad.
es.R: Hasta tus hermanos y el resto de tu familia \q se han puesto en tu contra. \q También ellos gritan contra ti. \q No confíes en ellos, aunque te digan cosas bonitas.

fr.L: Car même tes frères et la maison de ton père, \q même eux t’ont trahi ; \q même eux ont crié derrière toi à pleine [voix]. \q Ne te fie pas à eux, quand même ils te diraient de bonnes [paroles].
fr.B: Même tes frères, la famille de ton propre père, \q même eux t’ont trahi ; \q eux aussi crient à pleine voix contre toi. \q Ne les crois pas, même s’ils te parlent aimablement.
fr.R: Même tes frères et le reste de ta famille \q se sont retournés contre toi. \q Eux aussi crient contre toi. \q Ne leur fais pas confiance, même quand ils te disent des choses gentilles.

sw.L: Kwa maana hata ndugu zako na nyumba ya baba yako, \q hata wao wamekutendea kwa hila; \q hata wao wamekupigia kelele [kwa sauti] kuu nyuma yako. \q Usiwaamini, ingawa wanakuambia [maneno] mazuri.
sw.B: Hata ndugu zako, jamaa ya baba yako mwenyewe, \q hata wao wamekusaliti; \q wao pia wamepiga kelele kubwa dhidi yako. \q Usiwaamini, hata wanapokuambia maneno mazuri.
sw.R: Hata ndugu zako na jamaa yako yote \q wamegeuka dhidi yako. \q Wao pia wanakupigia kelele. \q Usiwaamini, hata wanapokuambia maneno mazuri.

vi.L: Vì ngay cả anh em và nhà cha ngươi, \q ngay cả chúng cũng đã phản bội ngươi; \q ngay cả chúng cũng đã lớn tiếng kêu la đuổi theo ngươi. \q Đừng tin chúng, dù chúng nói những lời tốt đẹp với ngươi.
vi.B: Ngay cả anh em con, gia đình của chính cha con, \q chúng cũng đã bội tín với con; \q chúng cũng đã lớn tiếng hô hoán chống lại con. \q Đừng tin chúng, dù chúng nói những lời tử tế với con.
vi.R: Ngay cả anh em con và những người khác trong gia đình con \q cũng đã quay lại chống con. \q Chúng cũng đang la lối chống lại con. \q Đừng tin chúng, ngay cả khi chúng nói những lời dễ nghe với con.

ko.L: 네 형제들과 네 아버지의 집, \q 그들조차 너를 배신했다. \q 그들조차 네 뒤에서 큰 소리로 외쳤다. \q 그들이 너에게 좋은 [말을] 해도 그들을 믿지 마라.
ko.B: 네 형제들, 네 아버지의 집안사람들까지도 \q 너를 배신했다. \q 그들까지도 너를 향해 크게 소리를 질렀다. \q 그들이 너에게 다정하게 말해도 그들을 믿지 마라.
ko.R: 네 형제들과 다른 가족들까지도 \q 너에게 등을 돌렸다. \q 그들도 너를 향해 소리를 지르고 있다. \q 그들이 너에게 좋은 말을 해도 그들을 믿지 마라.

decisions.choice: your brothers and your father's house: Jeremiah's own family
decisions.reason: Jeremiah came from a priestly family of Anathoth (1:1), and the men of Anathoth had plotted to kill him (11:21-23). Now God tells him that even his close relatives are part of it. "Dealt treacherously" is the word used of the wicked in verse 1.

decisions.choice: they have called after you in full: they have raised a loud outcry against you
alternatives: they have gathered a crowd against you
decisions.reason: The exact sense of "full" here is unclear. It may mean that they shout loudly after him, or that they have called a full crowd together against him (compare 4:5, where the same word means "aloud").

decisions.choice: the rest of your family
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the house of your father" as "family", which is what the phrase means.

source.text: עָזַ֨בְתִּי֙ אֶת־בֵּיתִ֔י נָטַ֖שְׁתִּי אֶת־נַחֲלָתִ֑י נָתַ֛תִּי אֶת־יְדִד֥וּת נַפְשִׁ֖י בְּכַ֥ף אֹיְבֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: I have forsaken my house; I have abandoned my inheritance; I have given [the] beloved of my soul into [the] palm of her enemies.

en.L: I have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house; \q I have abandoned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance; \q I have given the beloved of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul into [the] palm of her enemies.
en.B: I have left {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house; \q I have cast off {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance. \q I have handed the one I love with all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart over to her enemies.
en.R: I have left {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house. \q I have turned away from the people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I have handed the people I love so much over to their enemies.

es.L: He dejado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa; \q he desechado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} heredad; \q he entregado a la amada de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} alma en manos de sus enemigos.
es.B: He abandonado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa; \q he desechado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} heredad. \q He entregado a la que amo con todo {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón en manos de sus enemigos.
es.R: He abandonado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} casa. \q Me he apartado del pueblo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece. \q He entregado a la gente que tanto amo en manos de sus enemigos.

fr.L: J’ai abandonné {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison ; \q j’ai délaissé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} héritage ; \q j’ai livré la bien-aimée de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} âme dans la main de ses ennemis.
fr.B: J’ai quitté {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison ; \q j’ai rejeté {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} héritage. \q J’ai livré celle que j’aime de tout {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur aux mains de ses ennemis.
fr.R: J’ai quitté {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} maison. \q Je me suis détourné du peuple qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartient. \q J’ai livré le peuple que j’aime tant aux mains de ses ennemis.

sw.L: Nimeiacha nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q nimeutupa urithi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; \q nimemtia mpendwa wa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} katika kiganja cha adui zake.
sw.B: Nimeiacha nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q nimeukataa urithi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Nimemtia yule ninayempenda kwa moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wote mikononi mwa adui zake.
sw.R: Nimeiacha nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Nimewaacha watu walio mali {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Nimewatia watu ninaowapenda sana mikononi mwa adui zao.

vi.L: Ta đã lìa bỏ nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q Ta đã từ bỏ cơ nghiệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q Ta đã phó người yêu dấu của linh hồn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vào lòng bàn tay kẻ thù nó.
vi.B: Ta đã rời bỏ nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q Ta đã ruồng bỏ cơ nghiệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta đã trao người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hết lòng yêu dấu vào tay kẻ thù nó.
vi.R: Ta đã rời bỏ nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta đã quay lưng với dân thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Ta đã trao dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yêu quý vào tay kẻ thù của chúng.

ko.L: 내가 내 집을 버렸고, \q 내 유업을 내던졌다. \q 내 영혼이 사랑하는 자를 그 원수들의 손바닥에 넘겨주었다.
ko.B: 내가 내 집을 떠났고, \q 내 소유인 백성을 내버렸다. \q 내가 진심으로 사랑하는 백성을 그 원수들의 손에 넘겨주었다.
ko.R: 나는 내 집을 떠났다. \q 나는 나에게 속한 백성에게서 돌아섰다. \q 나는 내가 그토록 사랑하는 백성을 그들의 원수들에게 넘겨주었다.

decisions.choice: God speaks of his own people
decisions.reason: From here to verse 13 God himself laments what he has had to do. The verbs are in the past tense, as if the judgment had already happened, though it was still to come.

decisions.choice: my house ... my inheritance: God's people and land
decisions.reason: "House" may be the temple or, as often, the household of God's people; here it stands beside "inheritance", the people and land that belong to God as his own possession (2:7; 10:16; Deuteronomy 32:9).

decisions.choice: the beloved of my soul ... into the palm: the one I dearly love, into the power of
decisions.reason: "Soul" here means God's own self: the one he loves with all his being. "Into the palm of" means into someone's power. The people are pictured as a beloved woman, so "her enemies".

decisions.choice: the people who belong to me ... the people I love ... their enemies
decisions.reason: Readable explains "inheritance" and "beloved" as the people, and so says "their" for "her".

source.text: הָיְתָה־לִּ֥י נַחֲלָתִ֖י כְּאַרְיֵ֣ה בַיָּ֑עַר נָתְנָ֥ה עָלַ֛י בְּקוֹלָ֖הּ עַל־כֵּ֥ן שְׂנֵאתִֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Has become to me my inheritance like a lion in the forest; she has given against me with her voice; therefore I hate her.

en.L: My inheritance has become to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like a lion in the forest; \q she has raised her voice against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; therefore I hate her.
en.B: My inheritance has turned on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like a lion in the forest; \q she roars against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and so I have come to hate her.
en.R: The people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} have turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like a lion in the forest. \q They roar at {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So now I hate them.

es.L: Mi heredad ha venido a ser para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} como león en la selva; \q ha alzado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} su voz; por eso la aborrezco.
es.B: Mi heredad se ha vuelto contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} como un león en la selva; \q ruge contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y por eso he llegado a aborrecerla.
es.R: El pueblo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece se ha vuelto contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} como un león en la selva. \q Rugen contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Por eso ahora los aborrezco.

fr.L: Mon héritage est devenu pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} comme un lion dans la forêt ; \q il a élevé sa voix contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; c’est pourquoi je le hais.
fr.B: Mon héritage s’est retourné contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} comme un lion dans la forêt ; \q il rugit contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et j’en suis venu à le haïr.
fr.R: Le peuple qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartient s’est retourné contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} comme un lion dans la forêt. \q Il rugit contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Alors maintenant, je le hais.

sw.L: Urithi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umekuwa kwangu kama simba msituni; \q umepaza sauti yake dhidi yangu; kwa hiyo nimeuchukia.
sw.B: Urithi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umenigeukia kama simba msituni; \q unaningurumia, na kwa hiyo nimeuchukia.
sw.R: Watu walio mali {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} wamenigeukia kama simba msituni. \q Wananingurumia. Kwa hiyo sasa ninawachukia.

vi.L: Cơ nghiệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã trở nên đối với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như sư tử trong rừng; \q nó đã cất tiếng nghịch cùng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ghét nó.
vi.B: Cơ nghiệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã quay lại chống {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như sư tử trong rừng; \q nó gầm thét nghịch cùng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ghét nó.
vi.R: Dân thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã quay lại chống {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như sư tử trong rừng. \q Chúng gầm thét với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Vì vậy bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ghét chúng.

ko.L: 내 유업이 나에게 숲속의 사자처럼 되었다. \q 그것이 나를 향해 소리를 높이니 내가 그것을 미워한다.
ko.B: 내 소유인 백성이 숲속의 사자처럼 나에게 덤벼든다. \q 그들이 나를 향해 으르렁거리니 내가 그들을 미워하게 되었다.
ko.R: 나에게 속한 백성이 숲속의 사자처럼 나에게 맞선다. \q 그들이 나를 향해 으르렁거린다. 그래서 이제 나는 그들을 미워한다.

decisions.choice: like a lion ... gave her voice against me: the people roar at God like a hostile lion
decisions.reason: "To give the voice" is used of a lion roaring (2:15). The people God treasured have turned on him as a wild beast turns on a keeper.

decisions.choice: hate: reject, turn away from
decisions.reason: In covenant language "hate" can mean to reject or refuse to favor, set against "love" as choosing (Malachi 1:2-3; Hosea 9:15). God is not saying he has stopped caring (verse 7 still calls her "beloved"), but that he has withdrawn his protection.

decisions.choice: the people who belong to me ... them
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, Readable explains "my inheritance" as the people.

decisions.choice: "il" for "mon héritage"
decisions.reason: French "héritage" is masculine, so the pronouns follow it, where the Hebrew uses the feminine for the people.

source.text: הַעַ֨יִט צָב֤וּעַ נַחֲלָתִי֙ לִ֔י הַעַ֖יִט סָבִ֣יב עָלֶ֑יהָ לְכ֗וּ אִסְפ֛וּ כָּל־חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה הֵתָ֥יוּ לְאָכְלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] a speckled bird of prey my inheritance to me? [Are] birds of prey all around against her? Go, gather every animal of the field; bring [them] to devour.

en.L: [Is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a speckled bird of prey? \q [Are] birds of prey all around against her? \q Go, gather every animal of the field; bring [them] to devour.
en.B: Has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inheritance become to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a speckled bird of prey, \q set upon by birds of prey on every side? \q Go, gather all the wild animals; bring them to eat.
en.R: The people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} are like a bird with spotted feathers, \q and the other wild birds are all around it, attacking it. \q Go and gather all the wild animals. Bring them to eat.

es.L: ¿Es para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} heredad un ave de rapiña de muchos colores? \q ¿[Están] las aves de rapiña contra ella alrededor? \q {{plural_you:Vayan, reúnan|Id, reunid}} a todas las fieras del campo; {{plural_you:tráiganlas|traedlas}} a devorar.
es.B: ¿Se ha vuelto {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} heredad para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} un ave de rapiña de plumas pintas, \q atacada por las aves de rapiña de todos lados? \q {{plural_you:Vayan, reúnan|Id, reunid}} a todos los animales salvajes; {{plural_you:tráiganlos|traedlos}} a comer.
es.R: El pueblo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pertenece es como un ave de plumas manchadas, \q y las otras aves salvajes la rodean y la atacan. \q {{plural_you:Vayan y reúnan|Id y reunid}} a todos los animales salvajes. {{plural_you:Tráiganlos|Traedlos}} a comer.

fr.L: Mon héritage [est-il] pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} un oiseau de proie bigarré ? \q Les oiseaux de proie [sont-ils] tout autour contre lui ? \q Allez, rassemblez toutes les bêtes des champs ; amenez-[les] pour dévorer.
fr.B: Mon héritage est-il devenu pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} un oiseau de proie bigarré, \q que les rapaces attaquent de tous côtés ? \q Allez, rassemblez toutes les bêtes sauvages ; amenez-les pour qu’elles mangent.
fr.R: Le peuple qui {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartient est comme un oiseau aux plumes tachetées, \q et les autres oiseaux sauvages l’entourent pour l’attaquer. \q Allez rassembler toutes les bêtes sauvages. Amenez-les pour qu’elles mangent.

sw.L: Je, urithi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} [ni] kwangu ndege mla nyama mwenye madoadoa? \q [Je,] ndege wala nyama wako pande zote dhidi yake? \q Nendeni, wakusanyeni wanyama wote wa porini; waleteni wale.
sw.B: Je, urithi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umekuwa kwangu kama ndege mla nyama mwenye madoadoa, \q anayeshambuliwa na ndege wala nyama pande zote? \q Nendeni, wakusanyeni wanyama wote wa porini; waleteni wale.
sw.R: Watu walio mali {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni kama ndege mwenye manyoya ya madoadoa, \q na ndege wengine wa porini wamemzunguka wakimshambulia. \q Nendeni mkawakusanye wanyama wote wa porini. Waleteni wale.

vi.L: Cơ nghiệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đối với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [là] chim săn mồi có đốm sao? \q Chim săn mồi vây quanh nghịch cùng nó sao? \q Hãy đi, tập hợp mọi thú đồng; hãy đem [chúng] đến ăn nuốt.
vi.B: Cơ nghiệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã trở nên đối với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như một con chim săn mồi có đốm, \q bị chim săn mồi vây đánh tứ phía sao? \q Hãy đi tập hợp mọi thú hoang; hãy đem chúng đến ăn nuốt.
vi.R: Dân thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} giống như con chim có lông đốm, \q bị các loài chim hoang khác vây quanh tấn công. \q Hãy đi tập hợp mọi thú hoang. Hãy đem chúng đến mà ăn.

ko.L: 내 유업이 나에게 얼룩무늬 맹금이냐? \q 맹금들이 사방에서 그것을 노리느냐? \q 가서 들의 모든 짐승을 모아 와서 먹게 하여라.
ko.B: 내 소유인 백성이 나에게 얼룩무늬 맹금처럼 되어서 \q 사방에서 맹금들의 공격을 받는 것이냐? \q 가서 들짐승들을 다 모아 와서 먹게 하여라.
ko.R: 나에게 속한 백성은 깃털에 얼룩무늬가 있는 새와 같다. \q 다른 사나운 새들이 사방에서 그 새를 공격하고 있다. \q 가서 들짐승들을 모두 모아라. 와서 먹게 하여라.

decisions.choice: a speckled bird of prey
decisions.reason: The word rendered "speckled" (or "colored") is found only here. The picture seems to be of a bird with odd markings that the other birds of prey gang up on. The same letters can be read as "hyena", and the Greek translation speaks of a hyena's den; then the line would be "Is my inheritance a hyena's lair to me?"

decisions.choice: the questions expect the answer yes
decisions.reason: Both questions are of the kind that state something: God's people have become like a prey bird mobbed by others. The commands that follow call the wild animals to join the attack (compare Isaiah 56:9; Ezekiel 39:17).

decisions.choice: go, gather ... bring: commands to unnamed hearers
decisions.reason: The plural commands are not addressed to anyone named; they may be to the enemies of verse 7 or simply a call for the wild animals to come. Either way, the nations are pictured as beasts gathering to feed.

decisions.choice: questions turned into statements
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the questions mean (see m2).

source.text: רֹעִ֤ים רַבִּים֙ שִֽׁחֲת֣וּ כַרְמִ֔י בֹּסְס֖וּ אֶת־חֶלְקָתִ֑י נָֽתְנ֛וּ אֶת־חֶלְקַ֥ת חֶמְדָּתִ֖י לְמִדְבַּ֥ר שְׁמָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Shepherds many have ruined my vineyard; they have trampled my portion; they have made [the] portion of my delight into [a] wilderness of desolation.

en.L: Many shepherds have ruined {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard; \q they have trampled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} portion; \q they have made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} delightful portion into a wilderness of desolation.
en.B: Many shepherds have wrecked {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard \q and trampled down {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} field; \q they have turned the field I delight in into an empty wilderness.
en.R: Many rulers have ruined {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vineyard \q and trampled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} field. \q They have turned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} lovely field into an empty desert.

es.L: Muchos pastores han destruido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} viña; \q han pisoteado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} porción; \q han convertido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} porción deseable en desierto de desolación.
es.B: Muchos pastores han arruinado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} viña \q y han pisoteado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} campo; \q han convertido el campo en que me deleito en un desierto vacío.
es.R: Muchos gobernantes han arruinado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} viña \q y han pisoteado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} campo. \q Han convertido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hermoso campo en un desierto vacío.

fr.L: De nombreux bergers ont ravagé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} vigne ; \q ils ont piétiné {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} part ; \q ils ont fait de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} part délicieuse un désert de désolation.
fr.B: De nombreux bergers ont saccagé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} vigne \q et piétiné {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} champ ; \q ils ont fait du champ qui fait {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} délices un désert vide.
fr.R: Beaucoup de chefs ont détruit {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} vigne \q et piétiné {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} champ. \q Ils ont fait de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} beau champ un désert vide.

sw.L: Wachungaji wengi wameliharibu shamba {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} la mizabibu; \q wamelikanyaga fungu {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}; \q wamelifanya fungu {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} la kupendeza kuwa nyika ya ukiwa.
sw.B: Wachungaji wengi wameliharibu shamba {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} la mizabibu \q na kulikanyaga shamba {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}; \q wameligeuza shamba ninalolipenda kuwa nyika tupu.
sw.R: Watawala wengi wameliharibu shamba {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} la mizabibu \q na kulikanyaga shamba {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. \q Wamelifanya shamba {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} zuri kuwa jangwa tupu.

vi.L: Nhiều người chăn đã phá hoại vườn nho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q chúng đã giày đạp phần đất {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q chúng đã biến phần đất yêu quý của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành hoang mạc tiêu điều.
vi.B: Nhiều người chăn đã tàn phá vườn nho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và giày đạp ruộng đất {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q chúng đã biến ruộng đất {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yêu thích thành hoang mạc trống trải.
vi.R: Nhiều kẻ cai trị đã phá hoại vườn nho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và giày đạp ruộng đất {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Chúng đã biến ruộng đất xinh đẹp của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành sa mạc hoang vắng.

ko.L: 많은 목자들이 내 포도원을 망쳤고, \q 내 몫을 짓밟았으며, \q 내가 기뻐하는 몫을 황량한 광야로 만들었다.
ko.B: 많은 목자들이 내 포도원을 망가뜨리고 \q 내 밭을 짓밟았다. \q 내가 아끼는 밭을 텅 빈 광야로 만들었다.
ko.R: 많은 통치자들이 내 포도원을 망쳐 놓고 \q 내 밭을 짓밟았다. \q 그들이 나의 아름다운 밭을 텅 빈 사막으로 만들었다.

decisions.choice: many shepherds: rulers, here probably foreign kings and their armies
decisions.reason: "Shepherds" is a common picture for rulers (2:8; 23:1-4). In 6:3 shepherds with their flocks are enemy commanders camped around Jerusalem, and that fits here: invading kings who let their armies graze the land bare. Judah's own leaders are also called shepherds who ruined the flock (10:21; 23:1).

decisions.choice: my vineyard ... my portion: God's people and land
decisions.reason: Israel is God's vineyard in Isaiah 5:1-7 and Jeremiah 2:21. "Portion" is a plot of land, and the land is God's own share (Deuteronomy 32:9). "The portion of my delight" is the land God treasured (3:19).

decisions.choice: rulers
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the picture "shepherds" (see m1) and keeps the vineyard picture, which explains itself.

source.text: שָׂמָהּ֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֔ה אָבְלָ֥ה עָלַ֖י שְׁמֵמָ֑ה נָשַׁ֨מָּה֙ כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ שָׂ֥ם עַל־לֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: He has made it into [a] desolation; it mourns to me, desolate; desolate [is] all the land, for there is no man laying [it] on heart.

en.L: One has made it a desolation; \q it mourns to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, desolate. \q The whole land has been made desolate, \q for there is no one laying [it] to heart.
en.B: It has been made a desolation; \q ruined, it mourns before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q The whole land lies desolate, \q because no one takes it to heart.
en.R: The rulers have turned it into an empty waste. \q It lies ruined and cries to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in sorrow. \q The whole land has been ruined, \q but no one cares.

es.L: La han convertido en desolación; \q está de luto ante {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, desolada. \q Toda la tierra ha sido desolada, \q porque no hay nadie que [lo] tome a pecho.
es.B: Ha sido convertida en una desolación; \q arruinada, está de luto delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Toda la tierra está desolada, \q porque nadie se lo toma a pecho.
es.R: Los gobernantes la han convertido en un lugar vacío. \q Está arruinada y llora ante {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} con tristeza. \q Toda la tierra ha sido arruinada, \q pero a nadie le importa.

fr.L: On en a fait une désolation ; \q elle est en deuil devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, désolée. \q Tout le pays est dévasté, \q car personne ne [le] prend à cœur.
fr.B: On en a fait une désolation ; \q ravagée, elle est en deuil devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q Tout le pays est dévasté, \q parce que personne ne le prend à cœur.
fr.R: Les chefs en ont fait un lieu vide et désert. \q Elle est en ruine et pleure devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q Tout le pays est dévasté, \q mais personne ne s’en soucie.

sw.L: Mtu amelifanya kuwa ukiwa; \q linaomboleza kwangu, likiwa ukiwa. \q Nchi yote imefanywa ukiwa, \q kwa maana hakuna mtu anayeliweka moyoni.
sw.B: Limefanywa kuwa ukiwa; \q likiwa limeharibiwa, linaomboleza mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Nchi yote imekuwa ukiwa, \q kwa sababu hakuna anayelijali.
sw.R: Watawala wamelifanya kuwa jangwa tupu. \q Limeharibiwa na linanililia kwa huzuni. \q Nchi yote imeharibiwa, \q lakini hakuna anayejali.

vi.L: Người ta đã làm cho nó thành hoang vu; \q nó hoang tàn than khóc với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Cả xứ đã bị tàn phá, \q vì không ai để tâm [đến].
vi.B: Nó đã bị biến thành hoang vu; \q nó điêu tàn và than khóc trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Cả xứ đều hoang vắng, \q vì chẳng ai để tâm đến.
vi.R: Những kẻ cai trị đã biến nó thành nơi hoang phế. \q Nó nằm đó điêu tàn và khóc than với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Cả xứ đã bị tàn phá, \q nhưng chẳng ai quan tâm.

ko.L: 그가 그것을 황무지로 만들었다. \q 그것이 황폐하여 나에게 슬퍼한다. \q 온 땅이 황폐해졌으나 \q 마음에 두는 사람이 없다.
ko.B: 그 밭이 황무지가 되었다. \q 폐허가 되어 내 앞에서 슬퍼한다. \q 온 땅이 황폐해졌는데도 \q 아무도 그것을 마음에 두지 않는다.
ko.R: 통치자들이 그 밭을 텅 빈 황무지로 만들었다. \q 그 밭이 망가진 채 나에게 슬피 운다. \q 온 땅이 망가졌다. \q 그런데도 아무도 관심을 두지 않는다.

decisions.choice: he has made it: the doer is left general
decisions.reason: The verb has "he" as its subject without naming him. It most likely refers back to the shepherds of verse 10 as a group, or is used in a general way: "it has been made".

decisions.choice: desolation ... desolate ... made desolate: one root repeated
decisions.reason: Three words from the same root follow each other, hammering home the emptiness of the land. The land mourns (as in verse 4) while its people do not.

decisions.choice: laying it on heart: caring, paying attention
decisions.reason: To "put on the heart" means to give something serious thought and let it move you (Isaiah 42:25; 57:1).

decisions.choice: The rulers
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject from verse 10 (see m1).

decisions.choice: ukiwa ... ukiwa ... ukiwa
decisions.reason: One Hebrew root is repeated three times (meaning decision m2); Literal and Balanced keep the one word "ukiwa" each time.

source.text: עַֽל־כָּל־שְׁפָיִ֣ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר בָּ֚אוּ שֹֽׁדְדִ֔ים כִּ֣י חֶ֤רֶב לַֽיהוָה֙ אֹֽכְלָ֔ה מִקְצֵה־אֶ֖רֶץ וְעַד־קְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֥ין שָׁל֖וֹם לְכָל־בָּשָֽׂר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Upon all [the] bare heights in the wilderness have come destroyers, for [the] sword of Yahweh devours from [the] end of [the] land and to [the] end of the land; there is no peace for any flesh.

en.L: Upon all [the] bare heights in the wilderness destroyers have come, \q for [the] sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} devours from [one] end of the land to [the other] end of the land; \q there is no peace for any flesh.
en.B: Destroyers have swept over all the bare hills in the wilderness, \q for the sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is eating its way from one end of the land to the other; \q no living thing has peace.
en.R: Destroying armies have come over all the bare hills in the desert. \q The sword of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is killing people from one end of the land to the other. \q No one has any peace.

es.L: Sobre todas las alturas desnudas del desierto han venido destructores, \q porque la espada {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} devora desde un extremo de la tierra hasta el otro extremo de la tierra; \q no hay paz para ninguna carne.
es.B: Los destructores han invadido todas las colinas peladas del desierto, \q porque la espada {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} va devorando de un extremo a otro del país; \q ningún ser viviente tiene paz.
es.R: Ejércitos destructores han venido sobre todas las colinas peladas del desierto. \q La espada {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} está matando a la gente de un extremo a otro del país. \q Nadie tiene paz.

fr.L: Sur toutes les hauteurs dénudées du désert sont venus des dévastateurs, \q car l’épée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} dévore d’un bout du pays à l’autre bout du pays ; \q il n’y a pas de paix pour toute chair.
fr.B: Les dévastateurs ont déferlé sur toutes les collines dénudées du désert, \q car l’épée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} dévore d’un bout à l’autre du pays ; \q aucun être vivant n’a de paix.
fr.R: Des armées qui détruisent tout sont arrivées sur toutes les collines dénudées du désert. \q L’épée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} tue des gens d’un bout à l’autre du pays. \q Personne n’a de paix.

sw.L: Juu ya vilele vyote vilivyo wazi nyikani waharibifu wamekuja, \q kwa maana upanga wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} unakula kutoka mwisho [mmoja] wa nchi hata mwisho [mwingine] wa nchi; \q hakuna amani kwa mwenye mwili yeyote.
sw.B: Waharibifu wamepita juu ya vilima vyote vilivyo wazi nyikani, \q kwa maana upanga wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} unakula kutoka upande mmoja wa nchi hadi mwingine; \q hakuna kiumbe hai chenye amani.
sw.R: Majeshi yanayoangamiza yamekuja juu ya vilima vyote vilivyo wazi jangwani. \q Upanga wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} unaua watu kutoka upande mmoja wa nchi hadi mwingine. \q Hakuna mtu aliye na amani.

vi.L: Trên mọi đồi trọc trong hoang mạc, những kẻ hủy diệt đã đến, \q vì gươm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ăn nuốt từ đầu xứ này đến đầu xứ kia; \q không có bình an cho bất cứ loài xác thịt nào.
vi.B: Những kẻ hủy diệt đã tràn qua mọi đồi trọc trong hoang mạc, \q vì gươm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang ăn nuốt từ đầu xứ này đến đầu xứ kia; \q không sinh vật nào được bình an.
vi.R: Những đạo quân hủy diệt đã đến trên mọi đồi trọc trong sa mạc. \q Gươm của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang giết người từ đầu xứ này đến đầu xứ kia. \q Không ai được bình an.

ko.L: 광야의 모든 벌거숭이 언덕 위로 멸망시키는 자들이 왔다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 칼이 땅 이 끝에서 땅 저 끝까지 삼키니 \q 어떤 육체에게도 평안이 없다.
ko.B: 광야의 모든 민둥산 위로 약탈자들이 몰려왔다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 칼이 땅 이 끝에서 저 끝까지 삼키니 \q 살아 있는 것은 아무도 평안하지 못하다.
ko.R: 멸망시키는 군대들이 사막의 민둥산마다 몰려왔다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 칼이 땅 이 끝에서 저 끝까지 사람들을 죽이고 있다. \q 아무도 평안하지 못하다.

decisions.choice: bare heights: open hilltops, the routes invaders came by
decisions.reason: The word means windswept, bare hills (3:2, 21; 4:11). Destruction comes over the high ground into the land.

decisions.choice: the sword of the LORD devours: the invaders are God's instrument
decisions.reason: The armies are not acting on their own; it is God's sword that "eats" through the land (47:6; Deuteronomy 32:42). The speaker may be God speaking of himself by name, or the prophet taking up God's lament.

decisions.choice: the land: Judah, not the whole earth
decisions.reason: The same word can mean "land" or "earth". The context is the ruin of God's own land (verses 10-11), so the land of Judah is meant.

decisions.choice: no peace for any flesh: no living being is safe
decisions.reason: "All flesh" means every living creature, people above all. "Peace" here is safety and well-being.

decisions.choice: Destroying armies ... is killing people
decisions.reason: Readable says who the destroyers are and what the sword's "devouring" means.

source.text: זָרְע֤וּ חִטִּים֙ וְקֹצִ֣ים קָצָ֔רוּ נֶחְל֖וּ לֹ֣א יוֹעִ֑לוּ וּבֹ֨שׁוּ֙ מִתְּבוּאֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם מֵחֲר֖וֹן אַף־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: They have sown wheat and thorns they have reaped; they have exhausted themselves, they do not profit; and be ashamed of your harvests from [the] burning of [the] anger of Yahweh.

en.L: They have sown wheat, and thorns they have reaped; \q they have worn themselves out; they gain nothing. \q So be ashamed of your harvests \q because of the burning anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: They sowed wheat but reaped thorns; \q they wore themselves out for nothing. \q Be ashamed of your harvests, \q because of the fierce anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The people planted wheat, but they gathered only thorns. \q They worked until they were exhausted, but they gained nothing. \q So be ashamed of your harvests, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is burning with anger.

es.L: Sembraron trigo, y espinos segaron; \q se agotaron, y no sacaron provecho. \q {{plural_you:Avergüéncense|Avergonzaos}}, pues, de {{plural_you:sus cosechas|vuestras cosechas}} \q por el ardor de la ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Sembraron trigo, pero cosecharon espinos; \q se agotaron para nada. \q {{plural_you:Avergüéncense|Avergonzaos}} de {{plural_you:sus cosechas|vuestras cosechas}}, \q por la ardiente ira {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: La gente sembró trigo, pero solo recogió espinos. \q Trabajaron hasta quedar agotados, pero no ganaron nada. \q Así que {{plural_you:avergüéncense|avergonzaos}} de {{plural_you:sus cosechas|vuestras cosechas}}, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} arde de ira.

fr.L: Ils ont semé du blé, et ils ont moissonné des épines ; \q ils se sont épuisés, ils n’ont rien gagné. \q Ayez donc honte de vos récoltes, \q à cause de l’ardeur de la colère {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Ils ont semé du blé et moissonné des épines ; \q ils se sont épuisés pour rien. \q Ayez honte de vos récoltes, \q à cause de la colère ardente {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Les gens ont semé du blé, mais ils n’ont récolté que des épines. \q Ils ont travaillé jusqu’à l’épuisement, mais ils n’ont rien gagné. \q Alors ayez honte de vos récoltes, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} brûle de colère.

sw.L: Wamepanda ngano, na miiba wamevuna; \q wamejichosha, hawafaidiki. \q Basi aibikeni kwa mavuno yenu \q kwa sababu ya hasira kali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Walipanda ngano lakini wakavuna miiba; \q walijichosha bure. \q Aibikeni kwa mavuno yenu, \q kwa sababu ya hasira kali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Watu walipanda ngano, lakini wakavuna miiba tu. \q Walifanya kazi mpaka wakachoka, lakini hawakupata kitu. \q Kwa hiyo aibikeni kwa mavuno yenu, \q kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewaka hasira.

vi.L: Chúng đã gieo lúa mì, mà gặt gai góc; \q chúng đã làm cho mình kiệt sức mà chẳng được ích gì. \q Vậy hãy hổ thẹn về mùa màng của các ngươi \q vì cơn giận nóng cháy của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Chúng gieo lúa mì nhưng gặt gai góc; \q chúng làm lụng kiệt sức mà chẳng được gì. \q Hãy hổ thẹn về mùa màng của các ngươi, \q vì cơn giận dữ dội của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Dân chúng đã gieo lúa mì, nhưng chỉ gặt được gai góc. \q Họ làm việc đến kiệt sức, nhưng chẳng được gì. \q Vậy hãy hổ thẹn về mùa màng của các ngươi, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang nổi giận phừng phừng.

ko.L: 그들이 밀을 심었으나 가시를 거두었고, \q 애썼으나 아무 유익이 없다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 타오르는 분노 때문에 \q 너희는 너희 수확을 부끄러워하여라.
ko.B: 그들은 밀을 심고 가시를 거두었다. \q 애를 썼지만 헛수고였다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 맹렬한 분노 때문에 \q 너희는 너희 수확을 부끄러워하여라.
ko.R: 백성은 밀을 심었지만 가시만 거두었다. \q 그들은 지치도록 일했지만 아무것도 얻지 못했다. \q 그러니 너희 수확을 부끄러워하여라. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 몹시 노하고 계시기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: sowing wheat and reaping thorns: all their work comes to nothing
decisions.reason: It may describe the failed harvests of a ruined land, or be a saying about effort that ends in loss (compare Leviticus 26:20; Deuteronomy 28:38; Hosea 8:7; Micah 6:15).

decisions.choice: be ashamed of your harvests
alternatives: they will be ashamed of their harvests
decisions.reason: The form of the verb can be a command, "be ashamed", or a statement, "they are ashamed". "Your harvests" fits a command spoken directly to the people. Some read "they are ashamed of their harvests", keeping the third person of the first half; the sense is the same: disgrace at a failed harvest.

decisions.choice: the burning of the anger: fierce anger
decisions.reason: The phrase pairs a word for burning with the word for anger (literally "nose"), a common way of saying God's anger is fierce (4:8, 26; 25:37).

decisions.choice: The people
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, the people of the land.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל־כָּל־שְׁכֵנַי֙ הָֽרָעִ֔ים הַנֹּֽגְעִים֙ בַּֽנַּחֲלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הִנְחַ֥לְתִּי אֶת־עַמִּ֖י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנְנִ֤י נֹֽתְשָׁם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶתּ֥וֹשׁ מִתּוֹכָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh concerning all my neighbors, the evil [ones], who touch the inheritance which I caused to inherit my people Israel: here I [am] uprooting them from upon their land, and the house of Judah I will uproot from their midst.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} evil neighbors who touch the inheritance that I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel to inherit: Look, I am uprooting them from their land, and the house of Judah I will uproot from among them.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this concerning all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wicked neighbors who lay hands on the inheritance I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel to possess: Look, I am going to uproot them from their own soil, and the house of Judah I will uproot from their midst.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about all the wicked nations around Israel: They are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} neighbors, and they have attacked the land I gave {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel as their own. Now I am going to uproot those nations from their land. And I will uproot the people of Judah from among them.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca de todos {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} malos vecinos que tocan la heredad que hice heredar a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel: He aquí que yo los arranco de sobre su tierra, y a la casa de Judá arrancaré de en medio de ellos.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto acerca de todos {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} malvados vecinos que ponen la mano sobre la heredad que di en posesión a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel: Voy a arrancarlos de su propio suelo, y a la casa de Judá la arrancaré de en medio de ellos.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca de todas las naciones malvadas que rodean a Israel: Son {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} vecinos, y han atacado la tierra que di a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo Israel como suya. Ahora voy a arrancar a esas naciones de su tierra. Y arrancaré al pueblo de Judá de en medio de ellas.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au sujet de tous {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} méchants voisins qui touchent à l’héritage que j’ai fait hériter à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël : Voici, je vais les arracher de leur sol, et la maison de Juda, je l’arracherai du milieu d’eux.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci au sujet de tous {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} méchants voisins qui portent la main sur l’héritage que j’ai donné en possession à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël : Voici, je vais les arracher de leur propre sol, et la maison de Juda, je l’arracherai du milieu d’eux.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au sujet de toutes les nations méchantes qui entourent Israël : Ce sont {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} voisins, et elles ont attaqué le pays que j’ai donné à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple Israël comme sa propriété. Maintenant, je vais arracher ces nations de leur pays. Et j’arracherai le peuple de Juda du milieu d’elles.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi kuhusu jirani {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} wote waovu wanaougusa urithi niliowarithisha watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli: Tazama, ninawang'oa kutoka katika nchi yao, nayo nyumba ya Yuda nitaing'oa kutoka kati yao.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo kuhusu jirani {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} wote waovu wanaonyosha mikono juu ya urithi niliowapa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli wamiliki: Tazama, karibu nitawang'oa kutoka katika ardhi yao wenyewe, nayo nyumba ya Yuda nitaing'oa kutoka kati yao.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema kuhusu mataifa yote maovu yanayoizunguka Israeli: Ni jirani {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, nao wameishambulia nchi niliyowapa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Israeli iwe yao. Sasa nitayang'oa mataifa hayo kutoka katika nchi yao. Nami nitawang'oa watu wa Yuda kutoka kati yao.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này về mọi kẻ lân cận gian ác của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là những kẻ đụng đến sản nghiệp mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm cơ nghiệp: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhổ chúng khỏi đất của chúng, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhổ nhà Giu-đa ra khỏi giữa chúng.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy về mọi kẻ lân cận gian ác của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là những kẻ đã nhúng tay vào sản nghiệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm cơ nghiệp: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhổ chúng khỏi đất của chúng, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhổ nhà Giu-đa ra khỏi giữa chúng.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán về mọi dân tộc gian ác chung quanh Y-sơ-ra-ên: Chúng là láng giềng của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và chúng đã tấn công xứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm của riêng. Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhổ các dân tộc ấy khỏi đất của chúng. Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhổ dân Giu-đa ra khỏi giữa chúng.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내가 내 백성 이스라엘에게 유업으로 준 땅을 건드리는 나의 모든 악한 이웃에 대하여 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 보아라, 내가 그들을 그들의 땅에서 뽑아 버리고, 유다 집을 그들 가운데서 뽑아내겠다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 내 백성 이스라엘에게 유산으로 준 땅에 손을 대는 나의 모든 악한 이웃에게 말한다. 보아라, 내가 그들을 그들의 땅에서 뽑아 버리고, 유다 집을 그들 가운데서 뽑아내겠다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 주변의 모든 악한 민족들에 대하여 하시는 말씀이다. 그들은 내 이웃인데, 내가 내 백성 이스라엘에게 준 땅을 공격했다. 이제 내가 그 민족들을 그들의 땅에서 뽑아 버리겠다. 그리고 유다 백성을 그들 가운데서 뽑아내겠다.

decisions.choice: my evil neighbors: the nations around Israel
decisions.reason: The neighbors are the peoples on Judah's borders, such as Edom, Moab, Ammon and the Philistines, who raided the land and took part of it when Judah was weak (2 Kings 24:2; Ezekiel 25; 35). God calls them his own neighbors because the land is his.

decisions.choice: touch the inheritance: lay hands on it, seize or attack it
decisions.reason: The verb "touch" is used of harming or seizing (Genesis 26:11; Zechariah 2:12).

decisions.choice: uproot ... uproot: one verb for judgment and for rescue
decisions.reason: This is the first of the verbs of Jeremiah's call, "to uproot and to tear down" (1:10). The nations will be uprooted from their land in judgment, while Judah will be uprooted from among the nations where it has been taken, to be brought home. The same word is used for both.

decisions.choice: the change from prose to oracle
decisions.reason: Verses 14-17 are prose, not poetry. They widen God's lament over his own land (verses 7-13) to a promise about the nations around it.

decisions.choice: Look
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word that draws attention to what follows is "Look" at Literal and Balanced; Readable puts it as "Now".

decisions.choice: a long sentence split, and "neighbors" explained as nations
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence into short ones and says who the neighbors are (see m1).

decisions.choice: "arrancar"
decisions.reason: The verb of 1:10 ("arrancar"), kept for both uses here, the uprooting of the nations and the rescue of Judah, as the Hebrew uses one verb for both.

decisions.choice: kung'oa ... kung'oa
decisions.reason: One verb, "kung'oa", for uprooting the nations in judgment and uprooting Judah from among them in rescue (meaning decision m3), the first verb of the list in 1:10.

decisions.choice: "arracher" for *natash* (uproot), here and in verses 15-17
decisions.reason: The first verb of the list in 1:10 keeps its French wording wherever it returns, so the echo of Jeremiah's call is heard.

decisions.choice: "nhổ" (uproot) at every level
decisions.reason: The first verb of the list in 1:10, kept so the echo of Jeremiah's call is heard; here as there it is followed by building (verse 16).

decisions.choice: 뽑다 for "uproot", here and in verses 15 and 17
decisions.reason: The verb of the call (1:10) keeps its Korean form wherever it returns, so the echo can be heard.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה אַֽחֲרֵי֙ נָתְשִׁ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם אָשׁ֖וּב וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֑ים וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ לְנַחֲלָת֖וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ לְאַרְצֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, after my uprooting them, I will return and have compassion on them, and I will bring them back, each to his inheritance and each to his land.

en.L: And it will be, after I have uprooted them, I will turn back and have compassion on them, and I will bring them back, {{gender:each one to their|each man to his}} inheritance and {{gender:each one to their|each man to his}} land.
en.B: But after I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them, and I will bring them back, {{gender:each one to their own|each man to his own}} inheritance and {{gender:each one to their own|each man to his own}} land.
en.R: But after I have uprooted them, I will feel sorry for them again. I will bring them all back to their own property and their own land.

es.L: Y sucederá que, después de haberlos arrancado, volveré a tener compasión de ellos, y los haré volver, cada uno a su heredad y cada uno a su tierra.
es.B: Pero después de haberlos arrancado, volveré a tener compasión de ellos y los haré volver, cada uno a su propia heredad y cada uno a su propia tierra.
es.R: Pero después de arrancarlos, volveré a tener compasión de ellos. Los haré volver a todos a su propia heredad y a su propia tierra.

fr.L: Et il arrivera, après que je les aurai arrachés, je reviendrai et j’aurai compassion d’eux, et je les ramènerai, chacun dans son héritage et chacun dans son pays.
fr.B: Mais après les avoir arrachés, j’aurai de nouveau compassion d’eux, et je les ramènerai chacun dans son héritage et chacun dans son pays.
fr.R: Mais après les avoir arrachés, j’aurai de nouveau pitié d’eux. Je les ramènerai tous sur leur propriété et dans leur propre pays.

sw.L: Na itakuwa, baada ya kuwang'oa, nitarudi na kuwahurumia, nami nitawarudisha, kila mmoja kwenye urithi wake na kila mmoja kwenye nchi yake.
sw.B: Lakini baada ya kuwang'oa, nitawahurumia tena, nami nitawarudisha, kila mmoja kwenye urithi wake mwenyewe na kila mmoja kwenye nchi yake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Lakini baada ya kuwang'oa, nitawaonea huruma tena. Nitawarudisha wote kwenye mali zao wenyewe na nchi zao wenyewe.

vi.L: Sẽ xảy ra, sau khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nhổ chúng, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ quay lại và thương xót chúng, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đem chúng trở về, ai nấy về sản nghiệp mình và ai nấy về xứ mình.
vi.B: Nhưng sau khi đã nhổ chúng, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ lại thương xót chúng, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đem chúng trở về, ai nấy về với sản nghiệp riêng và xứ sở riêng của mình.
vi.R: Nhưng sau khi đã nhổ chúng, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ lại thương xót chúng. Ta sẽ đem tất cả chúng trở về với tài sản và đất đai riêng của mình.

ko.L: 내가 그들을 뽑아 버린 뒤에는 다시 그들을 불쌍히 여겨, 그들을 각자 자기 유업으로, 각자 자기 땅으로 돌아오게 하겠다.
ko.B: 그러나 내가 그들을 뽑아 버린 뒤에는 다시 그들을 불쌍히 여겨, 그들을 저마다 자기 유산으로, 저마다 자기 땅으로 돌아오게 하겠다.
ko.R: 그러나 내가 그들을 뽑아 버린 뒤에 나는 다시 그들을 불쌍히 여길 것이다. 나는 그들을 모두 자기 재산과 자기 땅으로 돌아오게 하겠다.

decisions.choice: them: the neighboring nations
decisions.reason: The "them" who are uprooted, pitied and brought back are the neighbors of verse 14. God's compassion reaches even the nations that harmed his people (compare 48:47; 49:6, 39).

decisions.choice: I will return and have compassion: I will again have compassion
decisions.reason: "Return" before another verb often means doing the thing again. God will turn from judgment back to mercy.

decisions.choice: feel sorry for them ... their own property
decisions.reason: Readable says "feel sorry for" for compassion and "property" for inheritance, the land each family held.

decisions.choice: "cada uno a su heredad", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "cada uno a su" serves for men and women alike, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: kila mmoja ... yake (no gender span)
decisions.reason: "Kila mmoja" and "yake" speak of anyone, man or woman, so the English gender spans have no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: "chacun dans son héritage", no gender span
decisions.reason: French "chacun ... son" is already generic, so the English gender spans have no counterpart.

source.text: וְהָיָ֡ה אִם־לָמֹ֣ד יִלְמְדוּ֩ אֶת־דַּֽרְכֵ֨י עַמִּ֜י לְהִשָּׁבֵ֤עַ בִּשְׁמִי֙ חַי־יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר לִמְּדוּ֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י לְהִשָּׁבֵ֖עַ בַּבָּ֑עַל וְנִבְנ֖וּ בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, if surely they learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, [by the] life of Yahweh, just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up in [the] midst of my people.

en.L: And it will be, if they truly learn the ways of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, to swear by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," just as they taught {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up in [the] midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.
en.B: And if they will truly learn the ways of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, swearing by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," as they themselves once taught {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people to swear by Baal, they will be built up in the midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.
en.R: Those nations once taught {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people to make promises in the name of Baal. But they may truly learn the ways of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people and make promises in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, saying, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives." If they do, they will be built up and given a place among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people.

es.L: Y sucederá que, si de veras aprenden los caminos de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, a jurar por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre: «Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}», así como enseñaron a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo a jurar por Baal, entonces serán edificados en medio de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo.
